title: Alternating Signal Length
statement: Given an integer sequence, find the length of its longest contiguous segment in which every adjacent pair has different values. A segment of length one is always valid. The sequence may contain negative values and duplicates. You must preserve the original order and may not delete elements to extend a segment. Print only the maximum length. A linear scan can maintain the current alternating segment length and reset it whenever two neighbors are equal.
reference_python:
import sys
d=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split())); n=d[0]; a=d[1:1+n]; cur=ans=1
for i in range(1,n):
 cur=cur+1 if a[i]!=a[i-1] else 1
 ans=max(ans,cur)
print(ans)

title: Stable Unique Sequence
statement: Read an integer sequence and remove repeated values while keeping only each value's first occurrence. Print the retained values in their original order. The values may be negative, and equal values are considered duplicates regardless of where they appear. If every value is distinct, the sequence remains unchanged. The task is not to sort the values: the first-seen order is part of the output. Use a membership structure to avoid repeatedly searching the retained prefix.

title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Group Ones
statement: A binary sequence contains zeroes and ones. In one operation, swap two adjacent elements. Find the minimum number of operations needed to make all ones form one contiguous block. The relative order of the ones does not matter, and zeroes may remain on either side. If there are fewer than two ones, the answer is zero. A useful observation is that a block containing every one must have length equal to the total number of ones; count the zeroes inside each window of that length.

title: Count Inversions
statement: An inversion is a pair of indices i and j such that i is before j but a[i] is greater than a[j]. Count all inversions in the given integer sequence. Equal values do not form an inversion. The answer can be much larger than the sequence length, so use integer arithmetic. A direct check of every pair is too slow for the maximum input size; a merge-based counting method can count cross-half inversions while sorting the sequence.
reference_python:
import sys
a=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()));a=a[1:];tmp=[0]*len(a)
def sort(l,r):
 if r-l<=1:return 0
 m=(l+r)//2;ans=sort(l,m)+sort(m,r);i,j,k=l,m,l
 while i<m and j<r:
  if a[i]<=a[j]:tmp[k]=a[i];i+=1
  else:tmp[k]=a[j];j+=1;ans+=m-i
  k+=1
 while i<m:tmp[k]=a[i];i+=1;k+=1
 while j<r:tmp[k]=a[j];j+=1;k+=1
 a[l:r]=tmp[l:r];return ans
print(sort(0,len(a)))
intended_complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

statement: Given a nonempty sequence of integers, find the maximum product of any nonempty contiguous segment. Values may be negative or zero, so the segment with the maximum product is not necessarily the one with the largest sum. Track both the largest and smallest products ending at the current position, because multiplying by a negative value can exchange their roles. title: Ways Through Blocked Grid
statement: A robot starts at the top-left cell of a rectangular grid and must reach the bottom-right cell. It may move only one cell right or one cell down. Some cells are blocked and cannot be entered; open cells are marked with a dot and blocked cells with a hash. Count the number of distinct valid paths. If the start or destination is blocked, the count is zero. Use exact integer arithmetic. Dynamic programming can reuse the counts from the cell above and the cell to the left without storing a full two-dimensional table.
input_format: r c; r strings of '.' and '#'

title: Edit Distance Between Labels
statement: Two labels are strings of lowercase English letters. One edit may insert a character, delete a character, or replace one character. Find the minimum number of edits needed to transform the first label into the second. Character order must be preserved, and each operation has cost one. If the strings are identical, the answer is zero. A dynamic programming state for prefixes considers the final operation: insertion, deletion, or replacement. The strings are bounded so a quadratic table is practical, though only the previous row needs to be retained.
reference_python:

s=sys.stdin.readline().strip();t=sys.stdin.readline().strip();prev=list(range(len(t)+1))
for i,x in enumerate(s,1):
 cur=[i]+[0]*len(t)
 for j,y in enumerate(t,1):cur[j]=min(cur[j-1]+1,prev[j]+1,prev[j-1]+(x!=y))
 prev=cur
print(prev[-1])

title: Bounded Knapsack Value
statement: A shopper has items with positive integer weights and nonnegative values and a bag with capacity W. Each item may be selected at most once. Find the maximum total value of a selection whose total weight does not exceed W. Items are distinct even if their weights and values match. The bag may remain partly empty. A one-dimensional dynamic program should process capacities in descending order for each item so that an item cannot accidentally be used more than once. Print the best attainable value.
input_format: n W; n lines weight value

statement: A set of sites must be connected using candidate undirected cables, each with a nonnegative installation cost. Choose a set of cables that connects every site with minimum total cost. statement: A directed acyclic graph has a start vertex s and a target vertex t. Every edge has a length that may be negative, zero, or positive. title: Run-Length Encode Token
statement: Compress a nonempty string by replacing each maximal run of identical adjacent characters with that character followed by the run length. Runs are written in the same order as they appear in the input. Include the count even when a character occurs only once. The input contains no whitespace, so every character belongs to the token. The output may be longer than the input for some strings, and no decoding is required. A single pass is enough to identify each run boundary.
reference_python:

while i<len(s):
 j=i+1
 while j<len(s) and s[j]==s[i]:j+=1
 out.append(s[i]+str(j-i));i=j
print(''.join(out))

title: Minimum Platforms Needed
statement: A railway station has train arrival and departure times on the same day, represented as integers. A platform is occupied from a train's arrival time through its departure time. If one train departs at the same time another arrives, the arriving train needs a separate platform because departure and arrival are treated as simultaneous occupancy. Arrival and departure lists correspond by train index, and each arrival is no later than its departure. Sorting the two event lists enables a linear sweep after sorting.

reference_python:

d=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()));n=d[0];a=sorted(d[1:1+n]);b=sorted(d[1+n:1+2*n]);i=j=cur=ans=0
while i<n:
 if a[i]<=b[j]:cur+=1;ans=max(ans,cur);i+=1
 else:cur-=1;j+=1
print(ans)
